mainTopic: סמיכה and תנופה with partners and on slaughtered animals, then the kneading, baking and molds of the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה: תנופה (waving) reaches further than סמיכה (placing hands), because it applies to slaughtered and non-living items too. A ברייתא learns from the word "קׇרְבָּנוֹ" that every owner of a קרבן must do סמיכה. Without that word, a קל וחומר from תנופה would have taught that one partner is enough. The גמרא then flips the קל וחומר to say every partner should also wave. It answers that this cannot be done: waving together creates a חציצה, and the תורה says one תנופה, not many. Next, a משנה about the כהן גדול leaning on slaughtered limbs seems to show סמיכה after שחיטה. אביי answers that this leaning is only for the כהן גדול's honor. The פרק שתי מדות then ends. A new משנה teaches how the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are kneaded, baked, and kept in molds, and the גמרא finds פסוקים for these rules and explains the three molds. The amud ends by asking what shape the לחם הפנים had, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Waving reaches live and slaughtered, living and non-living items
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה: תנופה applies to live and slaughtered offerings, and to living and non-living items. סמיכה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Waving is done with live animals and with slaughtered ones, and with things that have life and things that don't. This is not so with placing hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of ways that תנופה applies more widely than סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה is done on live animals, on parts of slaughtered animals, and even on non-living items like flour offerings or loaves. סמיכה is done only on a live animal. So in this respect תנופה has a wider reach.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing one's hands on the head of a live קרבן
Which is not so (in the other case)

phrases.english: with live animals and with slaughtered ones,
phrases.notes: The subject here is תנופה (waving), which the earlier part of the משנה started talking about.

phrases.english: and with something that has a living spirit
and with something that has no living spirit,
which is not so with placing hands.

steps.whatToRemember: תנופה applies more widely than סמיכה: it covers slaughtered and non-living items. סמיכה is only on a live animal. This fact is the base of the קל וחומר that comes next.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's comparison of the stringencies of תנופה and סמיכה from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנופה applies to live and slaughtered offerings and to living and non-living items. סמיכה does not.

steps.title: "His offering" includes every owner in placing hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word "קׇרְבָּנוֹ" that every owner of a קרבן must do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "His offering" comes to include all the owners of an offering in the duty of placing hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that finds a source in the פסוק that every partner in a קרבן must do סמיכה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "קׇרְבָּנוֹ" (his offering) is read as a רבוי, meaning it adds something. It teaches that each owner, not just one, must place his hands. This is the source for the משנה's rule that one person cannot do סמיכה for all the partners.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"His offering" —
comes to include all owners of an offering in placing hands.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that every partner in a shared קרבן must do סמיכה personally.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קׇרְבָּנוֹ – לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי קׇרְבָּן לִסְמִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rule about סמיכה with partners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every owner of a קרבן must do סמיכה, learned from "קׇרְבָּנוֹ".

steps.title: A logical argument that one partner should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows why the פסוק is needed: a קל וחומר from תנופה would have taught that one partner can do סמיכה for all.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might have said: isn't it logical? Waving was extended to slaughtered animals, yet it was limited with partners. Placing hands was not extended to slaughtered animals, so surely it should be limited with partners too.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why we need the פסוק. It shows that logic alone would have led to the opposite rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה is the wider מצוה, since it even applies to slaughtered animals. Still, one partner may wave for everyone. סמיכה is narrower, since it does not apply to slaughtered animals. So logic says it should certainly be limited, and one partner should be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? (opens a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: For one might have said: isn't it logical?
If waving, which was extended to slaughtered animals,
was limited with partners,
phrases.notes: Meaning one partner waves for all of them, as the משנה said earlier.

phrases.english: placing hands, which was not extended to slaughtered animals —
isn't it logical that it should be limited with partners?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final halacha. It is the "might have thought" that the פסוק comes to reject.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the derivation in step 2 is needed by showing the logic it overrides.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a פסוק to require every owner to do סמיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if the wider מצוה of תנופה is limited with partners, the narrower סמיכה should surely be limited too.

steps.title: The verse overrides the logic
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "קׇרְבָּנוֹ" overrides the קל וחומר and requires every owner to do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says "his offering," to include all owners of an offering in placing hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the logical argument by pointing to the פסוק, which says clearly that every owner must do סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic would have made one partner enough, so the תורה had to say it outright. The word "קׇרְבָּנוֹ" blocks the קל וחומר. The ברייתא repeats its opening words here to close the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says (a פסוק that settles the question)
For the duty of placing hands

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says "his offering,"
to include all owners of an offering in placing hands.

steps.whatToRemember: Every partner must do סמיכה. This comes from the פסוק "קׇרְבָּנוֹ", even though logic from תנופה pointed the other way.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 3 with the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An explicit פסוק overrides a logical קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One partner's סמיכה should be enough, like תנופה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every owner must do סמיכה because of "קׇרְבָּנוֹ".

steps.title: Flip it: maybe every partner must wave too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the קל וחומר around: if סמיכה needs every partner, then תנופה, the wider מצוה, should need every partner too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let waving be extended to partners by an a fortiori argument. Placing hands was not extended to slaughtered animals, yet it was extended to partners. Waving was extended to slaughtered animals, so surely it should be extended to partners too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that one partner may wave for all. It uses the new rule about סמיכה to build a קל וחומר in the opposite direction. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know from the פסוק that every partner must do סמיכה. סמיכה is the narrower מצוה, since it does not apply to slaughtered animals. So the wider מצוה, תנופה, should surely require every partner too. That would contradict the משנה, which says one partner waves for all.

keyTerms.meaning: By an a fortiori argument (from lighter to stronger)

phrases.english: But let waving be extended to partners by an a fortiori argument:
If placing hands, which was not extended to slaughtered animals,
was extended to partners,
then waving, which was extended to slaughtered animals —
isn't it logical that it is extended to partners!

steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of the direction. Step 3 used תנופה to limit סמיכה. Here the גמרא uses סמיכה to widen תנופה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 4 to build a reverse קל וחומר against the משנה's rule on תנופה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that one partner may wave for all the partners.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the narrower סמיכה requires every partner, the wider תנופה should require every partner too.

steps.title: Not every partner can wave, because there is no workable way to do it
steps.stepSummary: Every partner cannot do תנופה. Waving together would cause a חציצה, and waving one after another would make many wavings, while the תורה says one תנופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because it cannot be done. How would they do it? If all the partners wave together, there is a blocking (חציצה). If one waves and then another waves again, that does not work either, because the Merciful One said "a waving" and not "wavings."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. It explains why the קל וחומר cannot force every partner to do תנופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר is logical, but it runs into a practical wall. If everyone waves at once, their hands stack on each other, and the lower hands would block the upper ones (חציצה). If they take turns, there would be several wavings, but the תורה requires a single תנופה. So one partner waves for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible. Used to explain that a rule cannot apply because it cannot be carried out.
How would one do it? A way of showing that every option fails.
Something blocking direct contact between the person and the object. Here it makes the act invalid.
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳ as the source of the פסוק.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why סמיכה and תנופה end up with different rules for partners, even though the קל וחומר seemed to link them.

phrases.english: Because it is not possible,
phrases.notes: He means it cannot work for all the partners to wave.

phrases.english: how would they do it?
If all of them wave together,
there is a blocking.
phrases.notes: Their hands would be stacked, so the lower hands block the upper ones from touching the offering.

phrases.english: If one waves, and then another goes back and waves,
the Merciful One said "a waving,"
and not "wavings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reversed קל וחומר of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility: no valid way exists to carry out the act with every partner.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since סמיכה needs every owner, תנופה, the wider מצוה, should need every owner too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Group waving creates a חציצה, and waving in turns creates many wavings against the תורה's single תנופה. So one partner waves for all.

steps.title: A משנה shows the כהן גדול leaning on slaughtered limbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that סמיכה is not done on slaughtered animals. It quotes a משנה in which the כהן גדול does סמיכה on each cut limb before throwing it on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no סמיכה on slaughtered animals? But we learned in a משנה: When the כהן גדול wanted to burn the offering, he would go up the ramp with the סגן at his right. If he got halfway up, the סגן held his right hand and brought him up. The first כהן handed him the head and the leg, and he would lean his hands on them and throw them. The second כהן handed the two forelegs to the first, who gave them to the כהן גדול, and he would lean on them and throw them. The second כהן slipped away and left. In this way they handed him all the other limbs, and he would lean on them and throw them. And when he wanted, he would only lean, and others would throw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks a different line of the משנה: that סמיכה is not done on slaughtered animals. It brings a משנה that seems to show exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said סמיכה applies only to live animals. Yet in the quoted משנה the animal has already been slaughtered and cut into limbs, and the כהן גדול is described again and again as "סומך עליהם", leaning on those limbs. That looks like סמיכה on slaughtered pieces, which contradicts our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn the offering's parts on the altar.
The ramp leading up to the מזבח.
The deputy of the כהן גדול.
He throws them, meaning onto the altar fire.
The limbs or cut pieces of the offering.

steps.confusionAlert: The animal in the quoted משנה is already slaughtered and cut up. That is the whole point of the challenge: the word סומך is being used on dead pieces.

phrases.english: And is there no leaning of hands on slaughtered animals?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
When the High Priest wants to burn the offering,
he would go up the ramp,
with the deputy at his right.
If he reached halfway up the ramp,
the deputy held his right hand and brought him up.
And the first priest handed him
the head and the leg.
He leans his hands on them and throws them.
The second priest handed the two forelegs to the first,
who gives them to the High Priest.
He leans his hands on them and throws them.
The second priest slipped away and left.
And in this way they would hand him
all the rest of the limbs.
He leans his hands on them and throws them.
And when he wants,
he leans his hands, and others throw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תנופה discussion and challenges a different clause of the משנה from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that סמיכה is not done on slaughtered animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה describes the כהן גדול doing סמיכה (סומך עליהם) on the slaughtered, cut-up limbs before throwing them. This contradicts the claim that סמיכה applies only to live animals.

steps.title: The High Priest's leaning on limbs is only for his honor
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the כהן גדול's leaning on the cut limbs is not the מצוה of סמיכה. It is done only to honor the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There, it is done only because of the honor of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from Step 7. The leaning in that משנה is not real סמיכה, so the rule still stands: no סמיכה on a slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said the כהן גדול does סמיכה on slaughtered limbs. אביי says that act has a different purpose. It is not the קרבן's סמיכה at all. It just makes the כהן גדול's service more dignified, so it does not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other source

steps.whatToRemember: There is no סמיכה on a slaughtered animal. When the כהן גדול leans on the limbs, it is only a sign of honor, not the מצוה of סמיכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
There, it is because of the honor of the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי: התם משום כבודו דכהן גדול
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the act: the leaning is not the מצוה of סמיכה but a mark of honor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן גדול's leaning on the limbs shows that סמיכה can be done on a slaughtered animal
steps.terutzMaskana: That leaning is only for honor, so the rule of no סמיכה after שחיטה stands

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter שתי מדות
steps.stepSummary: The פרק שתי מדות comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שתי מדות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the פרק called שתי מדות. It is not part of the argument. It just marks that this chapter is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הדרן עלך are said when a פרק is finished. They express a hope to come back and learn it again. A new chapter starts right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is said when a chapter is finished.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Two Measures."
phrases.notes: "Two Measures" (שתי מדות) is the name of the chapter that just ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק שתי מדות is finished

steps.title: How the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are kneaded and baked
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches the kneading and baking order of the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים, and how the mold is used for the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שתי הלחם are kneaded one at a time and baked one at a time. The לחם הפנים are kneaded one at a time and baked two at a time. The baker made them in a mold. When he takes them out of the oven, he puts them back in a mold so they do not get ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It compares how two kinds of מנחה breads are prepared: the שתי הלחם of שבועות and the לחם הפנים of the שולחן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both breads are kneaded one loaf at a time. The difference is in the baking. The שתי הלחם go into the oven one at a time, but the לחם הפנים go in two at a time. The לחם הפנים also have a special shape, so a mold is used both before baking and after.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread: twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the מקדש
A mold that gives the bread its shape
Takes them out of the oven

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two breads. Both are kneaded one at a time. Only the baking is different: the שתי הלחם are baked one at a time, and the לחם הפנים two at a time.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The two loaves
are kneaded one by one,
and baked one by one.
The showbread loaves are kneaded one by one,
and baked two by two.
And he would make them in a mold;
when he takes them out of the oven, he places them in a mold
so that they will not be ruined.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ שתי הלחם נילושות אחת אחת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both breads are kneaded one at a time. The שתי הלחם are baked one at a time, and the לחם הפנים two at a time, shaped in a mold before and after baking.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the kneading and baking rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rules come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rules. This sets up the next step, where a ברייתא brings the answer from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated how each bread is kneaded and baked but did not give a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches these details.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? This asks for the source.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the kneading and baking order of the two breads

steps.title: The לחם הפנים are kneaded one loaf at a time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק "two tenths shall be in one loaf" that the לחם הפנים are kneaded one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "Two tenths of an איפה shall be in one loaf." This teaches that they are kneaded one at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The first part of the ברייתא learns from the פסוק that each loaf of the לחם הפנים is kneaded separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the amount of flour is for "one loaf." That shows each loaf gets its own measure and is kneaded on its own, not as part of one big dough. The ברייתא will go on to cover the שתי הלחם and the baking rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Tenths of an איפה, a measure of flour
A loaf or cake of bread
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"Two-tenths of an ephah shall be in one loaf"
teaches that they are kneaded one by one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתנו רבנן: שני עשרנים יהיה החלה האחת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "one loaf" in the פסוק teach that the לחם הפנים are kneaded one at a time

steps.title: The שתי הלחם are also kneaded one at a time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the שתי הלחם are also kneaded one at a time, learned from the word "יהיה".
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the שתי הלחם are also kneaded one at a time? The פסוק says "shall be."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It teaches that the rule of kneading one loaf at a time also applies to the שתי הלחם of שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 learned that the לחם הפנים are kneaded one at a time. Here the ברייתא extends that same rule to the שתי הלחם, using the word "יהיה" as its source.

keyTerms.meaning: "Shall be": the word used to include the שתי הלחם

phrases.english: From where do we know that the two loaves are also like this?
The verse teaches: "shall be."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 12 and extends its rule to the שתי הלחם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "יהיה" teaches that the שתי הלחם are also kneaded one at a time.

steps.title: The לחם הפנים are baked two at a time, but the שתי הלחם are not
steps.stepSummary: From "ושמת אותם" the ברייתא learns that the לחם הפנים are baked two at a time, and from "אותם" it learns that this does not apply to the שתי הלחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the לחם הפנים are baked two at a time? The פסוק says "and you shall set them." Could the שתי הלחם be the same? The פסוק says "them," meaning only these.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from kneading to baking. It says the לחם הפנים are baked two at a time, and that the שתי הלחם are not included in this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kneading was the same for both kinds of bread, but baking is different. The ברייתא uses the phrase "ושמת אותם" for the baking rule. It then uses the word "אותם" ("them," only these loaves) to leave out the שתי הלחם. This double use of "אותם" sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might think": opens a possible mistaken idea

phrases.english: And from where do we know that their baking is two at a time?
The verse teaches: "And you shall set them."
One might think the two loaves are also like this?
The verse teaches: "them."
phrases.notes: "Them" means these loaves only, which leaves out the שתי הלחם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues from kneading to baking.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "ושמת אותם" teaches baking two at a time for the לחם הפנים, and "אותם" leaves out the שתי הלחם.

steps.title: Wasn't the word "them" already used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the word "אותם" was already used to teach baking two at a time, so how can it also leave out the שתי הלחם?
steps.simpleTranslation: This word "them": didn't you already use it up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for using one word to teach two different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one word in a פסוק teaches one thing. The ברייתא used "אותם" first for baking two at a time and then again to leave out the שתי הלחם, which looks like using the same word twice.

keyTerms.meaning: "You took it out": you already used it for another teaching

phrases.english: This word "them": didn't you already use it?
phrases.notes: He means it was already used in the step before to teach baking two at a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the double use of "אותם" in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of "אותם" for two separate rules.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single word already used for one teaching cannot also be used for a second one.

steps.title: The long wording teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said the short "ושמתם". Writing the longer "ושמת אותם" shows that both rules are learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said "ושמתם." Why does it say "ושמת אותם"? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points out that the פסוק used longer wording than it needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hebrew can say "and you shall set them" in one word, "ושמתם". Since the פסוק splits it into two words, "ושמת אותם", the extra wording is enough to teach both rules: baking two at a time, and leaving out the שתי הלחם.

keyTerms.meaning: The short one-word form of "and you shall set them"

steps.whatToRemember: The extra wording "ושמת אותם" instead of "ושמתם" teaches two rules: the לחם הפנים are baked two at a time, and this does not apply to the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "and you shall set them" in one word!
What is meant by "and you shall set them" in two words?
Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows a double teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The longer wording "ושמת אותם" teaches both rules.

steps.title: The three molds used for the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that "ושמת אותם" means placing the loaves in a mold, and that three molds were used: one for the dough, one in the oven, and one after baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "and you shall set them" means in a mold. There are three molds. He puts the loaf in a mold while it is still dough. There was a kind of mold for it in the oven. When he takes it out, he puts it in a mold so it won't get ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא explains the משנה's mention of a mold. It lists the three molds the לחם הפנים went through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same phrase "ושמת אותם" is now read as a source for using a mold. The first mold shapes the dough, the second holds the loaf while it bakes, and the third protects the baked loaf's shape after it comes out of the oven.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "And you shall set them" means in a mold.
There are three molds:
He puts it in a mold while it is still dough,
and there was a kind of mold for it in the oven,
and when he takes it out, he puts it in a mold
so that it will not be ruined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the משנה's statement about the mold, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three molds were used for the לחם הפנים: for the dough, in the oven, and after baking.

steps.title: Why not reuse the first mold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a third mold is needed when the baked loaf could go back into the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him put it back into the first mold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for a third mold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first mold already has the right shape, so it seems wasteful to make another mold just for after baking.

phrases.english: But let him return it to the first mold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the third mold listed in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate third mold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first mold already exists and has the right shape, so a new one seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Baked bread swells
steps.stepSummary: Once the loaf is baked it swells, so it no longer fits the first mold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once it is baked, it swells.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the baked loaf is bigger than the dough was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough rises in the oven. The baked loaf no longer fits the small dough mold, so a larger mold is needed to protect its shape.

phrases.english: Once he bakes it, it swells.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first mold could be reused.
steps.terutzMaskana: The baked loaf has grown and no longer fits the first mold.

steps.title: What shape was the לחם הפנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic: how the לחם הפנים were made, meaning what shape they had.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: How do they make the לחם הפנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It raises the question of the loaves' shape, which will lead to a discussion of different views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "איתמר" usually introduces a dispute between אמוראים. Here it asks how the לחם הפנים looked, and the answers come in the next part of the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: The shewbread placed on the שולחן in the מקדש

phrases.english: It was stated:
The shewbread, how do they make it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים, כֵּיצַד עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the molds to the loaves' shape.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The shape in which the לחם הפנים were made.
